sentence_stem: If I had known about the delay,
correct_completion: I would have taken an earlier train.
full_sentence: If I had known about the delay, I would have taken an earlier train.
acceptable_variants: I would have left home sooner.
I would have caught a different train.

options.text: I take an earlier train every day.
options.why_wrong: The present simple describes a habit and does not match the unreal past 'had known' that the sentence sets up.

options.text: I have taken an earlier train before.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect describes a past experience. It does not express the imagined result of a condition that did not happen.

options.text: I would have taken an earlier train.
I will have taken an earlier train.
options.why_wrong: The future perfect refers to a completed action in the future, so it does not fit a hypothetical past condition.

grammar_focus: Third conditional with 'would have' in the main clause
explanation: The 'if' clause uses the past perfect to describe an unreal past condition. The main clause must then use 'would have' plus the past participle to show the imagined result. Turkish speakers may use a simple past here, but English needs the perfect form in both clauses.
